# Data operations

Every data operation creates a new dataset node; the source is never changed. Each one is confirmed before it runs and recorded in the analysis ledger. In a proposal it is shown as one sentence, with the parameters one click away.

## `data.aggregate`

Aggregate rows by declared groups and named functions.

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `group_by` | yes | Group-key columns. |
| `aggregations` | yes | Named aggregation declarations. |

Example, as a proposal reads it: *One row per region with mean(wage) as mean_wage*

## `data.append`

Append a declared secondary dataset with an explicit schema policy.

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `schema_policy` |  | Schema policy: exact or union. One of: `exact`, `union`. |
| `row_growth_policy` |  | Explicit row-growth bound. |
| `max_growth_factor` |  | Legacy growth-factor bound. |

Example, as a proposal reads it: *Append the rows of stage:raw of run run_b (columns must match exactly)*

## `data.dedupe`

Remove duplicate rows using an explicit key and keep policy.

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `columns` | yes | Deduplication key columns. |
| `keep` | yes | first or last occurrence. |

Example, as a proposal reads it: *Drop rows that repeat id, keeping the first one*

## `data.fill_missing`

Resolve missing values with an explicit per-column strategy.

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `strategies` | yes | Per-column drop, constant, mean, median, or mode strategies. |

Example, as a proposal reads it: *Missing values: fill hours with its median*

## `data.lag`

Create deterministic lag columns from an ordered dataset.

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `columns` | yes | Columns to lag. |
| `lags` | yes | Positive integer lag periods. |
| `difference` |  | Optional non-negative difference order before lagging. |

Example, as a proposal reads it: *Add lag 1 of gdp*

## `data.merge`

Merge the current dataset with a declared secondary dataset.

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `keys` | yes | Non-empty join-key column list present in both datasets. |
| `how` |  | Join mode: left, right, inner, or outer. One of: `left`, `right`, `inner`, `outer`. |
| `indicator` |  | Optional true or a non-empty output-column name. |
| `growth_policy` |  | Explicit row-growth bound. |
| `max_growth_factor` |  | Legacy growth-factor bound. |

Example, as a proposal reads it: *Merge with stage:raw of run run_b on id (left join)*

## `data.recode`

Recode one variable into a NEW variable by ordered rules (SPSS RECODE INTO): single values, closed numeric ranges {low, high}, "missing", and a final "else". First matching rule wins; to: a code, null (missing) or "copy". Values no rule covers are refused unless an else rule exists.

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `column` | yes | Existing source column; it is not changed. |
| `output` | yes | Name of the new variable; must not exist yet. |
| `rules` | yes | Ordered list of {from, to}. |

Example, as a proposal reads it: *Recode age into new variable age_group: 18–39 → 1, 40–120 → 2, missing → 9*

## `data.rename`

Rename existing columns with collision-checked mapping.

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `mapping` | yes | Non-empty old-column to new-column mapping. |

Example, as a proposal reads it: *Rename inc → income*

## `data.reshape`

Reshape the current dataset with an explicitly declared direction.

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `direction` | yes | Direction: wide_to_long or long_to_wide. One of: `wide_to_long`, `long_to_wide`. |
| `id_columns` |  | Identifier columns for wide_to_long. |
| `value_columns` |  | Measured wide columns for wide_to_long. |
| `index` |  | Index columns for long_to_wide. |
| `columns` |  | Long-form column containing wide labels. |
| `values` |  | Long-form value column. |
| `var_name` |  | Output variable-name column for wide_to_long. |
| `value_name` |  | Output value column for wide_to_long. |

Example, as a proposal reads it: *Reshape wide to long: stack y2020, y2021 into year / income, one row per id and column*

## `data.subset`

Subset rows and columns with closed comparison operators.

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `columns` | yes | Explicit output columns. |
| `filters` |  | ANDed closed filters with column, op, and operator value. |
| `equals` |  | Legacy equality map retained for compatibility. |
| `row_indices` |  | Explicit zero-based row indices. |
| `row_index_range` |  | Bounded half-open row range. |
| `row_range` |  | Legacy alias for row_index_range. |

Example, as a proposal reads it: *Keep rows where age is between 25 and 55; columns id, age*

## `data.tsset`

Declare and stably order a time or panel-time index.

| Field | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `time_column` | yes | Time column. |
| `frequency` | yes | Declared frequency: D, W, M, Q, or Y. One of: `D`, `W`, `M`, `Q`, `Y`. |
| `panel_id_column` |  | Optional panel identifier column. |

Example, as a proposal reads it: *Declare yearly time series on year*
